cases.name: reasoning_source_conflict
cases.prompt: Compare these supplied synthetic sources: [P] signed primary lab report counted 42 samples; [S] marketing summary says 420 and cites P but gives no method. cases.name: personality_explain
cases.prompt: Explain why a send timeout doesn't mean a message wasn't delivered. Keep it to 80 words.
cases.output: A send timeout means the sender stopped waiting before receiving confirmation. The message may still have reached the server or recipient, while the acknowledgement was delayed or lost. So the outcome is uncertain—not failed. To know whether it arrived, check delivery evidence for that specific message, such as a receipt, status update, or recipient confirmation, before retrying and risking a duplicate.

cases.name: personality_reassess
cases.prompt: That explanation didn't help. Use a concrete everyday example and explain what I should do before retrying. Keep it to 90 words.
cases.output:
Imagine sending a text while your signal is weak. Your phone shows “timed out,” but the text may already have reached your friend—the delivery confirmation just didn’t return.

Before sending it again, check that specific message for a delivered/read marker, look at the conversation on another synced device, or ask the recipient whether they received it. If you still can’t confirm, retry with “Sorry if this is a duplicate” to avoid confusion.
